items.title: Repeat the tense particle or leave it out

states.label: Particle repeated
states.sm: Sā timu ma sā lolo le vai.
states.en: It rained and the water overflowed.
states.note: The second clause repeats the first clause’s tense particle.

states.label: Particle absent
states.sm: Sā timu ma lolo le vai.
states.en: It rained and the water overflowed.
states.note: The second clause has no tense particle. The empty slot is a valid form.

items.caption: Both shapes are printed and both are good Samoan. The chapter treats the choice as style rather than meaning.

items.title: Sort the links between clauses

bins.label: While: events held together in time

items.sm: ʻUa ala le tama ma ʻua usu le teine.
items.en: The boy has woken and the girl has stood up.

items.sm: Na taunuʻu mai le pasi ma na alu le teine ʻi le āʻoga.
items.en: The bus arrived and the girl went to the school.
items.why: The clauses are joined by *ma* and repeat the same past particle.

items.sm: ʻUa ala le teine ʻae ʻoloʻo moe le tama.
items.en: The girl has woken but the boy is sleeping.
items.why: *ʻAe* opens the second clause and sets it against the first.

items.sm: Na usu le teine ʻaʻo moe le tama.
items.en: The girl stood up while the boy slept.
items.why: *ʻAʻo* holds the two events side by side in time.

items.intro: Choose the kind of link the joining word makes between the two clauses.

items.title: Two ways to say before

states.label: With *ʻaʻo leʻi*
states.sm: Na taunuʻu mai le pasi ʻaʻo leʻi tā=ina le ono.
states.en: The bus arrived before six o'clock.

states.label: With *ʻae leʻi*
states.sm: Na taunuʻu mai le pasi ʻae leʻi tā=ina le ono.
states.en: The bus arrived before six o'clock.

items.caption: Either combination says that the second event had not happened yet when the first occurred. English gathers that relationship into before.
